items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: They had a pianist, his name was Toya(?)... I don't know whether that was his first name or last name -- Toya(?)

ctx.x: One in particular was a big guy that always impressed me as being a typical laborer-looking type fellow, big arms, strong. Everybody called him Kid Norfolk. And Kid Norfolk, I think, could play in maybe one or two keys, F or F-sharp or C-sharp. And he would sit down and he would really make that piano ring. Most of the pianos were old upright pianos then, and he had this very strong left hand, and being physically strong himself, you could hear him all through the neighborhood. And people would come, and even…

Then there were other pianists. There was another fellow, Kid Socks(?), who played very good piano in that particular what they called House Hop style. Then there were a couple of other pianists that occasionally would come into these places who had a little better status. They were with a group... I remember a group called the Four Dots that was very popular around here, and they used to broadcast on the radio once a week. They had a pianist, his name was Toya(?). I
